note: Built-in collections and their starting members. The Prohibition list is drinks created or first recorded during US Prohibition (16 Jan 1920 - 5 Dec 1933), plus the Daiquiri (popularised then), each with a source; Bloody Mary and Mimosa are left out because neither is documented until after repeal.

collections.name: Prohibition
collections.title: Prohibition
collections.description: Drinks created or first recorded during US Prohibition (1920–1933), each with its story and a source.

members.name: Bee's Knees
members.note: 1929: First printed in Paris in 1929 (Cocktails de Paris, credited to Frank Meier of the Ritz); the popular 'honey masked bathtub gin' speakeasy story comes from Embury and is not supported.

members.name: Mary Pickford
members.note: 1920s (printed 1928): Created at the Hotel Nacional in Havana for the film star during Prohibition and printed in Basil Woon's 1928 When It's Cocktail Time in Cuba; the bartender credit (Fred Kaufman or Eddie Woelke) is disputed.

members.name: Boulevardier
members.note: 1927: Credited to American expat writer Erskine Gwynne at Harry MacElhone's bar in Paris, first printed in Barflies and Cocktails (1927).

members.name: Monkey Gland
members.note: c. 1922–23: Harry MacElhone's Paris drink named after Voronoff's rejuvenation experiments; in his ABC of Mixing Cocktails from 1922/1923.

members.name: Sidecar
members.note: first printed 1922: First printed in 1922 (Vermeire and MacElhone), usually credited to Pat MacGarry of Buck's Club, London, which opened in 1919; Embury's claim that it dates to WWI makes the exact creation date disputed.

members.name: Paradise
members.note: 1922: First appeared in MacElhone's 1922 Harry's ABC of Mixing Cocktails and was refined in Craddock's 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.

members.name: Between the Sheets
members.note: 1920s (printed 1929): First printed in 1929 (Frank Shay) and linked to a speakeasy in a 1930 newspaper column; one claim credits the Berkeley Hotel, London, in 1921.

members.name: Corpse Reviver #2
members.note: first recorded 1930: 'Corpse reviver' is an old name for a type of drink, but the No. 2 recipe (gin, Cointreau, Kina Lillet, lemon, absinthe) is first recorded in the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.

members.name: Angel Face
members.note: first recorded 1930: First appears in Harry Craddock's 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.

members.name: Hanky Panky
members.note: c. 1921: Made by Ada Coleman at the Savoy for actor Charles Hawtrey, probably around 1921, and printed in the 1930 Savoy book; Difford's also says 'early 1900s', so the date is not certain.

members.name: White Lady
members.note: c. 1929 (gin version): MacElhone's 1919 White Lady used crème de menthe; today's gin, Cointreau and lemon version appears around 1929 (credited to MacElhone, Craddock or Victor Cabrin) and was printed in the 1930 Savoy book.

members.name: French 75
members.note: 1927 (modern gin & Champagne form): The name dates to WWI (a different 1915 recipe with applejack and grenadine); the gin, lemon, sugar and Champagne version first appears in Judge Jr.'s 1927 Here's How, a Prohibition-era US book.

members.name: Alexander
members.note: first recorded 1930 (brandy version): The original 1916 Alexander used gin; the cognac version that IBA lists first appears in the 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book.

members.name: Remember the Maine
members.note: 1933 (printed 1939): Charles H. Baker recorded drinking it in Havana during the 1933 Cuban revolution, before repeal, and printed it in The Gentleman's Companion (1939).

members.name: Mojito
members.note: name first recorded 1931: The name 'Mojito' first appears on Sloppy Joe's Havana menu for 1931-32, though earlier forms were printed in 1927 and 1929 and the Draque goes back much further; American visitors during Prohibition are thought to have shaped it.

members.name: Pisco Sour
members.note: first recorded 1920: The earliest mention by name is in the Peruvian magazine Hogar (September 1920), tied to American expat Victor Morris's Lima bar, but a similar unnamed recipe dates to 1903 and there is no link to US drinking.

members.name: Daiquiri
members.note: 1890s: Popularised by American mining engineer Jennings Cox in Cuba in the 1890s, it was refined in Havana bars like El Floridita for American drinkers who went there during Prohibition.

members.name: Honolulu Cocktail No. 1
members.note: first recorded 1930: Gin with pineapple, orange and lemon juice and bitters, adapted from Harry Craddock's 1930 Savoy Cocktail Book; no earlier source was found, but it may predate 1930.
